clue.text: Sailor afraid of fever?

parts.note: yellow is an old word for cowardly or afraid
Jack (Jack Tar) is a traditional name for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman who dreads catching some tropical illness.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse of the clue's order: the cowardly colour first, then the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow jack is an old nautical name for yellow fever, from the quarantine flag ships flew.

clue.text: The French lion's hair brought up to a glossy coat

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the letters of both pieces are read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: le is the French for the
a lion's mane is its hair

explanation.surface: A lion's mane is groomed until it shines like a lacquered finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns the whole of LEMANE, giving ENAMEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a hard shiny surface layer, as on pottery or teeth.

clue.text: Sound of early riser's feline contentment in bed?

indicators.note: sound of says the words that follow are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a lark is someone who rises early, from the bird singing at dawn; a cat purrs when content

explanation.surface: A cat purrs happily under the covers beside its early-rising owner.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by place: something found in a flower bed, not a person under the sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a garden flower, the annual delphinium, grown in borders and beds.

clue.text: Hatchet-wielder was falsifying nothing

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: falsifying means distorting, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone with an axe claims there was nothing false in what he said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falsifying' rearranges NOTHING into HINGTON. The surface plays on the legend that the young president could not tell a lie about chopping the cherry tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend has George Washington as a boy chopping down his father's cherry tree with a hatchet.

clue.text: Contribution to Italy's summer flower show

indicators.note: Contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An entry from Italy to a summer flower show.
explanation.definitionFit: Alyssum is a low-growing garden plant with small white or purple blooms.

clue.text: Johnson's pastern on which he would submit he erred

definitions.text: Johnson's pastern on which he would submit he erred

parts.words: Johnson's pastern on which he would submit he erred
parts.note: Dr Johnson's dictionary wrongly defined a horse's pastern as this joint, and one goes down on it to submit or confess

explanation.surface: Dr Johnson admits his famous dictionary blunder over a horse's leg.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Johnson's 1755 dictionary called the pastern this part of a horse; asked why, he answered 'Ignorance, madam, pure ignorance.' Kneeling is the posture of submission.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson's error named the leg joint that one bends to kneel in submission.

clue.text: The case for a take-away?

parts.note: a grammatical case expressing removal or separation, the meaning of 'taking away', not a box for carry-out food

explanation.surface: A container for carrying home a meal from a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' and 'take-away' suggest food packaging; the case is grammatical, the Latin one meaning 'from' or 'away'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin ablative case expresses separation, its name coming from the Latin for 'carried away'.

clue.text: Permission to proceed on the starboard side

explanation.surface: A sailor gets the go-ahead to move off on the right-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: A go signal is permission to start; ships carry a lamp of this colour on the right-hand side.

clue.text: Singular or plural, when it's up you've had it

definitions.text: when it's up you've had it

explanation.surface: A grammar question meets a grim warning that time has run out.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammatical number is singular or plural; 'your number's up' means your time has come.

clue.text: Part of church, say, in which King Charles has one canonized

indicators.note: in which says the word say is opened and the other pieces placed inside

parts.note: taken as written
CR is Carolus Rex, the royal cipher of King Charles
I is the Roman numeral for one
ST is the abbreviation for saint, someone canonized

explanation.surface: A church where Charles I, made a saint, is honoured.
explanation.walkthrough: King Charles the Martyr was treated as a saint by the Church of England, which sharpens the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacristy is the room in a church where vestments and sacred vessels are kept.

clue.text: Cheapest way to travel always in the theatre

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the stage means the theatre as a profession
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Someone who always takes the cheap seats at the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the lowest-priced passenger accommodation on a ship.

clue.text: Fast speed needed to make things fast

explanation.surface: Hurrying is needed to secure things firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip is a brisk pace, and also a fastener that holds things together.

clue.text: The Mikado finds one horse-dealer in 'stupor

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a coma is a deep stupor
I is the Roman numeral for one
a coper is an old word for a horse dealer

explanation.surface: An emperor discovers a horse trader in a daze.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mikado is the Gilbert and Sullivan work, not a Japanese emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's Mikado is a classic example of a light, humorous stage work set to music.

clue.text: Dancer's extraordinary hurling act

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer gives a remarkable display of throwing.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautch girl is a professional dancing girl of India.

clue.text: Conchy's out, teased as being fair game

indicators.note: teased means pulled apart, as fibres are, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored and the S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A conscientious objector has been released and is mocked as an easy target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teased' rearranges CONCHYSOUT. A conchy is old slang for a conscientious objector; the surface's 'fair game' means a legitimate target.
explanation.definitionFit: A coconut shy is a fairground stall where balls are thrown at nuts, literally a game at the fair.

clue.text: Some birds do so with the speed of Russian aircraft

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter jet
rate means speed

explanation.surface: Birds fly as fast as Soviet jets.
explanation.definitionFit: Many birds travel seasonally between regions, which is the verb for that journey.

clue.text: Fuzzy Frenchman right in end-game variation

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the rearranged letters
a variation is a changed version, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French chess player tries a different finish to his game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation' rearranges ENDGAME, and R goes inside. 'Fuzzy' is from 'the fuzz', slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a French policeman, and 'the fuzz' is slang for police.

clue.text: Main cause of the 1912 disaster

parts.note: the main is the sea, and the 1912 disaster is the sinking of the Titanic, struck by a floating mass

explanation.surface: Asking what chiefly brought about a famous shipwreck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' reads as 'chief' but is the old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titanic sank in 1912 after striking a huge floating block of frozen water.

clue.text: Party with outlandish beard and pigtail, say?

parts.note: barbe is the French word for beard, and outlandish means foreign

indicators.note: say means spoken, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a queue is an old word for a pigtail of hair

explanation.surface: A gathering where someone turns up with a strange beard and plaited hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbecue is an outdoor social gathering with food grilled over a fire.

clue.text: He provides not only Chinese diners with chopsticks

definitions.text: He provides not only Chinese diners with chopsticks

parts.words: He provides not only Chinese diners with chopsticks
parts.note: Chopsticks is a simple tune played on the keyboard, so the provider is a musician, not a waiter

explanation.surface: A restaurant worker hands out eating sticks to customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopsticks' is the beginner's waltz played with two fingers on the keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard player is the one who performs the tune called Chopsticks.

clue.text: Protocol in assembly?

explanation.surface: Rules of etiquette observed at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A convention is both an accepted custom and a formal gathering of delegates.

clue.text: Fled before onset of the storm

indicators.note: before says the first piece comes ahead of the next

parts.note: ran means fled

indicators.note: onset of means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone escaped just as the bad weather began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' reads as weather but is the definition, a verb meaning to rage; the T comes from 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm is to shout angrily, to rage at length.

clue.text: From Turin a new sort of fur

indicators.note: new sort of means a fresh arrangement of the letters before it

explanation.surface: An Italian city produces a novel kind of fur.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutria is the pelt of the coypu, a South American rodent.

clue.text: Scheme king has not rejected for simple life at sea

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A king who has not turned down a scheme for a simple life on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are the tiny drifting organisms, plant and animal, of the ocean.

clue.text: Journey's End, about end of war

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a tip is an end, as of a finger

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Journey's End is the play about the close of the First World War.
explanation.walkthrough: Journey's End is R. C. Sherriff's First World War play; 'Journey's' is the definition with 's for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a journey or excursion.

clue.text: How to protect property round city district when liable to be burgled

indicators.note: round means placed around the other piece

parts.note: to insure is to protect property with a policy
EC is the postcode district for the City of London

explanation.surface: Advice on guarding your home when it is at risk from thieves.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the London postcode area covering the City.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insecure is unprotected and so open to theft or attack.

clue.text: I am at home in island state on the Adriatic

indicators.note: in says those pieces go inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: RI is Rhode Island, a US state
I'm is short for I am
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone is at home on an island somewhere in the Adriatic.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'island state' is American, Rhode Island, not an Adriatic island.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is an Italian seaside resort on the Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Minor award for a glazier?

parts.note: a joke prize for something trivial, imagined as made of the window-fixing paste a glazier uses

explanation.surface: Asking what small honour a window fitter might receive.
explanation.definitionFit: A putty medal is a humorous name for a worthless reward for trivial service.
